newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends narrowly weaker in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends narrowly weaker in thin trade.

text.p: IPE Brent crude sagged on Friday to end narrowly weaker as dealers cashed in profits made during the week's gasoline-led rally.
Uncertainty over near-term direction for the NYMEX unleaded contract made for choppy conditions in later dealing as European holidays sidelined many players and kept volumes thin.
Oct Brent settled at $19.01 a barrel, down five cents on the day but well above the session low of $18.83.
"The locals tried to push it through $19.05 but there wasn't enough momentum to keep it up there," said a broker.
The Oct contract touched $19.07 briefly before easing back.
Dealers said Brent was due to consolidate after rallying from $18.40 a barrel at Monday's open and some saw signs that the summer gasoline season may be beginning to falter.

Tight U.S. markets have been drawing product out of Europe and helping keep refinery margins strong and although demand remains strong, it has started to slip, according to the latest U.S. inventory data.
The imminent return to normal production of Tosco's giant Bayway catalytic cracker, shut since the end of July, would also help ease the supply situation.
Providing some fundamental support to Brent was news of lower North Sea loadings from the eight main exports systems, seen down 280,000 barrels per day (bpd) in September from the this month.
Earlier, IPE Sept gas oil settled at $171.50 a tonne, down $2.25 from Thursday's close but above the intraday low of $170.00. Dealers said gas oil futures were lifted by the upturn in crude.
